summary: The candidate ran the tests, read the failing test, and within a minute correctly named the exact mechanism (sweep releasing original count instead of remaining), then made a single scoped edit that turned the suite green and gave a root-cause explanation matching the planted bug. The session was fast and efficient with light but sufficient narration at each key juncture.

dimensions.analysis: They did not ask the interviewer any clarifying questions, but they did read the failing test body and quoted its expected-vs-actual values before forming a direction, which resolved the relevant ambiguity through the material itself rather than through guessing. This falls short of actively surfacing the partial-shipment edge case out loud, but it is not an unstated assumption either.

Before touching any code, they stated a specific, falsifiable mechanism — the sweep releases the original unit count rather than the remaining count — which matches the ground-truth root cause almost verbatim. This is a mechanism, not just a location, and it was stated prior to the edit.

The transcript alone tracks their path: diagnosing the diff at +30s, naming the mechanism at +60s, and explaining the root cause at +145s. Though sparse, each narration point lands exactly at a decision moment, letting an interviewer follow the reasoning without needing to interrupt.

The edit to src/sweep.ts directly followed from the stated hypothesis about released quantity, was saved promptly, and was scoped to the single file implicated by the bug — no scattered or contradictory edits appeared.
After editing, they re-ran the full test suite and confirmed a pass before declaring the issue resolved, treating the green run as confirmation rather than skipping straight to a claim of success.
Their closing statement ties the fix back to the mechanism — phantom stock from returning the original count — rather than just noting the tests passed, matching the actual root cause of the bug.
